Comment: Outside ROI: noROI(input) - Vestibular sensory input source. Receives primary vestibular afferents and sends secondary vestibulocerebellar fibers to cerebellum. Includes medial lateral descending and superior vestibular nuclei. Encodes head velocity/acceleration and efference copy of eye movement commands.
Output Semantics: Head velocity and acceleration information and efference copy of eye movement commands;

Comment: Outside ROI: noROI(input) - Visual motion information input source. Relays information from visual cortex and frontal eye fields via mossy fibers to cerebellum. Encodes visual motion information (optic flow).
Output Semantics: Visual motion information (optic flow) and information from visual cortex and frontal eye fields;

Names: Nucleus of the optic tract / Accessory optic system
Comment: Outside ROI: noROI(input) - Visual error signal input source. Detects retinal slip and projects to inferior olive. Shows direction selectivity for slow visual motion. Pre-stage for error signal generation.
Output Semantics: Retinal slip encoded in direction-selective manner as visual error information;

Comment: Outside ROI: noROI(input) - Error signal (teaching signal) input source. Integrates visual error signals and projects via climbing fibers to Purkinje cells. Provides teaching signals that induce synaptic plasticity. Includes subnuclei such as dorsomedial cell column and beta-nucleus.
Output Semantics: VOR error signals based on retinal slip error (teaching signals) and instructive signals that induce synaptic plasticity;

Comment: Inside ROI - Located in cerebellar cortex granular layer. Receives vestibular and visual motion information via mossy fibers and sends axons as parallel fibers to molecular layer. Only excitatory interneurons in cerebellar cortex. Responsible for encoding and expansion of sensory information.
Output Semantics: Temporally and spatially filtered multisensory integrated information (conjunctive representation of vestibular and visual motion information);
Requirement: To realize VOR learning it is necessary to integrate input head motion information from [U.VN-input] and input visual motion information from [U.PN] and generate temporally and spatially filtered multisensory integrated representations as output [U.PF] through inhibitory modulation by [U.GoC]. This transformation enables [U.PC] downstream to execute synaptic plasticity in appropriate sensory context. Note: Output Semantics are explicitly stated for involved Uniform Circuits.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface receives different sensory modality inputs from [U.VN-input] and [U.PN] and inhibitory feedback from [U.GoC] with output to [U.PF]. This makes the multisensory integration and spatiotemporal filtering required by Requirement realizable. The combination of inputs provides the sensory context needed for VOR learning.
Capability: Capability to integrate different sensory modalities (vestibular visual) and perform expansion recoding into high-dimensional representational space under inhibitory gain control. Each granule cell randomly integrates approximately 4 different sensory inputs and generates sparse activity patterns (sparse coding) thereby realizing pattern separation (Cayco-Gajic et al. 2023; Nature Comm. Biol. 2023). This capability enables associative learning downstream.
Mechanism: Granule cells receive multiple mossy fiber inputs via dendritic claws and fire when simultaneous inputs exceed threshold. GABAergic inhibition from Golgi cells sparsifies granule cell population activity and limits overlap between sensory ensembles. This inhibition is recruited in stimulus-specific manner and decorrelates multisensory ensembles. Approximately 100-fold expansion (number of granule cells vs mossy fibers) embeds input patterns in high-dimensional space improving linear separability (kernel machine perspective Frontiers Comp. Neurosci. 2022).
Implementation: [U.GrC] = Theta(Sum w_mf * [U.VN-input] + Sum w_pn * [U.PN] - [U.GoC]) where Theta is threshold function and w_mf w_pn are input weights

Comment: Inside ROI - Inhibitory interneurons located in granular layer. Receive excitatory inputs from mossy fibers and parallel fibers and provide GABAergic inhibition to granule cells. Responsible for spatiotemporal gain modulation of granule cell-parallel fiber pathway through feedforward and feedback inhibition.
Output Semantics: Inhibitory gain control signals that temporally and spatially modulate granular layer activity;
Requirement: In VOR learning it is necessary to integrate excitatory inputs from inputs [U.VN-input] [U.PN] and [U.PF] and generate inhibitory gain control signals to output [U.GrC] thereby temporally and spatially modulating granule cell population activity. This realizes sparse coding of granule cells and control of timing and variability of information transfer. By optimizing activity sparseness of output [U.GrC] this supports efficient learning at [U.PC]. Note: Output Semantics explicitly stated for involved circuits.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface receives feedforward inputs from [U.VN-input] and [U.PN] and feedback input from [U.PF] with inhibitory output to [U.GrC]. This structure realizes both feedforward and feedback inhibition required by Requirement enabling spatiotemporal modulation of granule cell activity.
Capability: Capability to integrate excitatory inputs from different pathways and perform inhibitory gain control and timing modulation to target neural populations. Golgi cells receive functionally distinct mossy fiber inputs compared to granule cells enabling pathway-specific control (bioRxiv 2024). Moderate inhibition levels optimize pattern separation performance with feedforward and feedback inhibitory circuits exerting distinct effects on coding expansion and decorrelation (Nature Sci. Rep. 2025).
Mechanism: Golgi cells integrate excitatory inputs from mossy fibers and parallel fibers and execute GABAergic inhibition to granule cell dendrites within cerebellar glomeruli. This inhibition acts through two mechanisms: phasic inhibition (alpha1-GABA-A receptor-mediated) via synaptic vesicular GABA release and tonic inhibition (alpha6-GABA-A receptor-mediated) via ambient GABA (Frontiers Cell. Neurosci. 2014). The timing of inhibition improves reproducibility across granule cell population while reducing individual spike precision controlling temporal fidelity of information transfer (J. Neurosci. 2024).
Implementation: [U.GoC] = f(Sum w_mf * ([U.VN-input] + [U.PN]) + Sum w_pf * [U.PF]) where f is activation function

Comment: Inside ROI - Fibers formed by bifurcation of granule cell axons in T-shape in molecular layer. Provide excitatory inputs to Purkinje cell dendrites and molecular layer interneurons. Transmit sensory information widely to Purkinje cells realizing information conjunction.
Output Semantics: Spatially distributed multisensory integrated information (extensive conjunctive patterns of vestibular and visual motion information);
Requirement: In VOR learning it is necessary to spatially distribute and transmit sparse multisensory integrated information from input [U.GrC] to outputs [U.PC] [U.BC] [U.SC] [U.GoC]. This distribution enables each [U.PC] to receive diverse sensory context information via approximately 100000 parallel fiber synapses enabling conjunctive learning required for VOR adaptation. Projections to [U.BC] and [U.SC] drive lateral inhibition circuits and feedback to [U.GoC] realizes inhibitory modulation. Note: Output Semantics explicitly stated.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface shows one-to-many structure with single input from [U.GrC] branching to multiple downstream targets ([U.PC] [U.BC] [U.SC] [U.GoC]). This structure realizes spatial distribution and simultaneous driving of diverse downstream circuits required by Requirement. The physical spatial extent of parallel fibers supports this functional distribution.
Capability: Capability to spatially distribute information from single granule cell to hundreds to thousands of downstream neurons transmitting high-dimensional information patterns. Each parallel fiber extends several millimeters in molecular layer intersecting dendritic trees of many Purkinje cells along its path. This structure enables each Purkinje cell to receive synaptic inputs from over 100000 different parallel fibers representing vast numbers of sensory conjunction patterns. This geometric arrangement provides foundation for cerebellum to function as kernel machine.
Mechanism: Parallel fibers are generated by T-shaped bifurcation of granule cell axons. Each parallel fiber forms excitatory glutamatergic synapses on Purkinje cell dendrites encountered along its trajectory. Synaptic transmission is mediated by AMPA receptors and mGlu1 receptors generating fast currents and slow signals respectively (Frontiers Synaptic Neurosci. 2016). The geometric arrangement of parallel fibers enables information from same granule cell to reach multiple spatially separated Purkinje cells simultaneously enabling parallel information processing.
Implementation: [U.PC] = Sum_i [U.PF]_i [U.BC] = Sum_j [U.PF]_j [U.SC] = Sum_k [U.PF]_k [U.GoC] = Sum_l [U.PF]_l (each downstream target receives inputs from different subsets of parallel fibers)

Comment: Inside ROI - Inhibitory interneurons located in deep molecular layer. Receive excitatory inputs from parallel fibers and provide GABAergic inhibition around initial segments of Purkinje cell axons. Mediate lateral inhibition and sharpen Purkinje cell output patterns.
Output Semantics: Lateral inhibition signals that sharpen Purkinje cell output patterns;
Requirement: In VOR learning it is necessary to detect spatial activity patterns of input [U.PF] and perform inhibition around initial segments of output [U.PC] thereby sharpening Purkinje cell output patterns. This lateral inhibition suppresses inactive Purkinje cells around active ones improving spatial contrast of output signals and increasing precision of VOR adjustment signals. Optimizes correspondence between activity patterns of [U.PF] and output patterns of [U.PC]. Note: Output Semantics explicitly stated.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface receives excitatory input from [U.PF] and produces inhibitory output to [U.PC]. This structure realizes detection of parallel fiber activity patterns and lateral inhibition to Purkinje cells required by Requirement. The feedforward inhibitory circuit structure supports output pattern sharpening.
Capability: Capability to detect excitatory input patterns from parallel fibers and execute feedforward lateral inhibition to target neuron populations. Basket cells are excited along trajectory of activated parallel fibers and provide strong GABAergic inhibition to axon initial segments of nearby Purkinje cells. This inhibition shapes response dynamics of Purkinje cell populations realizing winner-take-all computation rather than simple blocking (Frontiers Mol. Neurosci. 2019).
Mechanism: Basket cells have cell bodies in deep molecular layer and receive excitatory glutamatergic inputs from parallel fibers. Basket cell axons extend transversely across folium forming basket-like synaptic contacts around initial segments of multiple Purkinje cell axons. Here GABA is released powerfully suppressing action potential generation in Purkinje cells. This inhibition selectively suppresses Purkinje cells located on both sides of active parallel fiber beam relatively enhancing output of centrally activated Purkinje cells.
Implementation: [U.BC] = f([U.PF]) [U.PC]_inhibited = [U.PC]_original - w_bc * [U.BC] where w_bc is inhibitory weight depending on lateral position

Comment: Inside ROI - Inhibitory interneurons located in molecular layer. Receive excitatory inputs from parallel fibers and provide GABAergic inhibition to Purkinje cell dendrites. Mediate lateral inhibition and modulate information integration in Purkinje cell dendrites.
Output Semantics: Lateral inhibition signals that modulate information integration in Purkinje cell dendrites;
Requirement: In VOR learning it is necessary to detect activity patterns of input [U.PF] and perform inhibition on dendrites of output [U.PC] thereby modulating information integration in Purkinje cell dendrites. This inhibition selectively modulates spatiotemporal patterns of parallel fiber inputs integrated by Purkinje cells optimizing integration efficiency of [U.PF] inputs at [U.PC]. Works in coordination with [U.BC] to shape input-output relationships of Purkinje cells. Note: Output Semantics explicitly stated.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface receives excitatory input from [U.PF] and produces inhibitory output to [U.PC]. This structure realizes detection of parallel fiber activity and dendritic level inhibition required by Requirement. The position of inhibition on dendrites enables modulation of input integration function.
Capability: Capability to detect parallel fiber activity and execute feedforward inhibition on Purkinje cell dendrites thereby locally modulating dendritic information integration. Stellate cells are located more superficially in molecular layer than basket cells and provide GABAergic inhibition to Purkinje cell dendrites. This inhibition modulates integration of excitatory inputs in dendrites controlling dendritic compartment computation. Cerebellar inhibitory interneurons complexly shape neuronal response dynamics rather than simply blocking excitation (Frontiers Mol. Neurosci. 2019).
Mechanism: Stellate cells are located in molecular layer and receive excitatory inputs from parallel fibers. Their axons form GABAergic synapses on Purkinje cell dendrites providing local inhibition. This inhibition shapes spatial and temporal patterns of parallel fiber inputs received by Purkinje cells modulating nonlinear computation in dendrites. While basket cells control output at axon initial segment stellate cells control input integration at dendrites thereby multilayerally modulating input-output relationships of Purkinje cells.
Implementation: [U.SC] = f([U.PF]) [U.PC]_dendrite = ([U.PF]_input - w_sc * [U.SC]) * g_dendrite where w_sc is inhibitory weight and g_dendrite is dendritic integration function

Comment: Inside ROI - Principal output neurons of cerebellar cortex. Receive massive excitatory inputs from parallel fibers single powerful excitatory input (error signal) from climbing fibers and inhibitory inputs from basket/stellate cells. Provide GABAergic inhibitory projections to vestibular nuclei and modulate VOR gain. Plasticity (LTD/LTP) at parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synapses is primary mechanism of VOR learning.
Output Semantics: Adaptively modulated VOR inhibitory signals through learning and gain modulation signals for vestibulo-ocular transformation;
Requirement: In VOR learning it is necessary to integrate multisensory information from input [U.PF] error signals from input [U.IO] and lateral inhibition signals from inputs [U.BC] and [U.SC] to generate inhibitory signals to output [U.VN-output]. When error signals from [U.IO] arrive via climbing fibers simultaneous activation with [U.PF] induces plasticity (LTD or LTP) at parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synapses adaptively modulating VOR gain. This learning optimizes inhibition to [U.VN-output] improving compensation accuracy of eye movements for head motion. Note: Output Semantics explicitly stated for all involved circuits.
Requirement realization by interface: The Interface receives massive excitatory inputs from [U.PF] single powerful teaching signal from [U.IO] and inhibitory modulation signals from [U.BC] and [U.SC] with output to [U.VN-output]. This structure realizes multi-input integration and learning-dependent output modulation required by Requirement. Particularly the structure where simultaneous activation of [U.PF] and [U.IO] induces synaptic plasticity provides neural substrate for VOR learning.
Capability: Capability to integrate large-scale excitatory inputs and adaptively modulate synaptic weights based on error signals thereby learning input-output transformations. Purkinje cells execute long-term depression (LTD) and long-term potentiation (LTP) at parallel fiber-Purkinje cell synapses realizing motor learning. LTD mediates gain decrease while LTP mediates gain increase (Broussard & Titley 2013). Complex spikes via climbing fibers function as teaching signals inducing Hebbian or anti-Hebbian plasticity for simultaneous activation patterns of parallel fibers (Najafi et al. 2024). This supervised learning mechanism is core of Marr-Albus-Ito theory.
Mechanism: At synapses between parallel fibers and Purkinje cell dendrites mGluR1 activation and IP3 generation by parallel fiber stimulation and voltage-gated calcium channel (VGCC) opening and calcium influx by climbing fiber stimulation are integrated at IP3 receptors. This coincidence detection activates protein kinase C (PKC) which phosphorylates AMPA receptors causing their removal by endocytosis producing LTD (Nature Rev. Neurosci. 2002). Conversely high-frequency parallel fiber stimulation induces LTP increasing AMPA receptors. This bidirectional plasticity enables VOR gain to be modulated in both increase and decrease directions. Purkinje cells provide GABAergic inhibitory projections to vestibular nuclei and changes in inhibition strength modulate VOR gain.
Implementation: [U.PC] = Sum_i w_i(t) * [U.PF]_i - w_bc * [U.BC] - w_sc * [U.SC] Plasticity rule: dw_i/dt = eta * [U.IO] * ([U.PF]_i - theta) where w_i(t) is time-dependent synaptic weight eta is learning rate theta is threshold

Comment: Outside ROI: noROI(output) - Output target receiving VOR motor command modulation. Receives inhibitory projections from Purkinje cells and projects to extraocular motor nuclei (abducens oculomotor trochlear). Realizes final adjustment of VOR gain generating adaptive eye movements. Same vestibular nuclei as VN-input but functions as output in information processing flow.
Output Semantics: Adaptively modulated VOR motor commands and control signals to extraocular muscles;

Comment: Outside ROI: noROI(output) - One of extraocular motor nuclei. Receives excitatory input from vestibular nuclei and innervates lateral rectus muscle. Executes horizontal VOR.
Outside ROI: noROI(output) - One of extraocular motor nuclei. Receives input from vestibular nuclei and controls vertical and torsional eye movements.
Outside ROI: noROI(output) - One of extraocular motor nuclei. Receives input from vestibular nuclei and innervates superior oblique muscle. Controls vertical and torsional eye movements.
